questions.question: 1. Which of the following is the best case time complexity of bubble sort?

explanations.a: Correct. Bubble sort is O(n) in the best case when the array is already sorted.
explanations.b: Incorrect. O(n^2) is the average and worst case.
explanations.c: Incorrect. O(log n) is not for bubble sort.
explanations.d: Incorrect. O(n log n) is for merge/quick sort.

questions.question: 2. Which searching algorithm divides the search interval in half each time?

explanations.a: Correct. Binary search halves the interval each step.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Linear search checks each element.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Jump search skips ahead by fixed steps.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Exponential search expands the interval exponentially.

questions.question: 3. Which sorting algorithm is NOT stable?

explanations.b: Correct. Selection sort is not stable in general.

questions.question: 4. What is the main advantage of merge sort over bubble sort?

answers.a: Merge sort is easier to implement
answers.b: Merge sort is faster for large data

explanations.a: Incorrect. Merge sort is more complex to implement.
explanations.b: Correct. Merge sort is much faster for large datasets.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Merge sort uses more memory.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Bubble sort is slower for large data.

questions.question: 5. Which searching algorithm is best for unbounded or infinite lists?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Linear search is not efficient for large/unbounded lists.
explanations.c: Correct. Exponential search is designed for unbounded lists.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Jump search is for bounded lists.

questions.question: 6. Which of the following statements about sorting is TRUE?

answers.a: Bubble sort is always faster than quick sort.
answers.b: Merge sort is stable and efficient for large data.
answers.c: Selection sort is the fastest algorithm.
answers.d: Insertion sort is always O(n log n).

explanations.a: Incorrect. Bubble sort is slower than quick sort.
explanations.b: Correct. Merge sort is stable and efficient for large data.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Selection sort is not the fastest.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Insertion sort is O(n^2) in general.
